newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end 6.0 pct up but off highs.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end 6.0 pct up but off highs.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures soared by six percent by the close basis March on persistent fund buying although trade-related sales shaved some earlier gains.
"The market is in bullish frame of mind," said one trader. "The Brazilian news sparked it off."
The market as expected propelled sharply higher at the start on the back of impressive New York close the day before on forecasts of a lower 1997/98 Brazilian coffee crop released on Monday.
The benchmark March contract climbed to a high of $1,473 a tonne at one stage, up seven percent on the day and the highest since September, on heavy fund shortcovering.
By the close, the actively-traded March and May were each $80 firmer at $1,460.
Brazilian officials on Monday put the country's 1997/98 crop at between 18-20 million 60-kg bags against 25 million in 1996/97.

But traders said Tuesday comments by a former U.S. Department of Agriculture crop watcher that a majority of Brazilian coffee trees inspected in October and November by him showed signs of recovery from the 1994 frosts were seen as less bullish.
Traders said most producers stepped back on Tuesday as the market soared.
London's market also found further strength on Monday on news Vietnam was considering joining the producer-only group's export programme.
But Vietnamese industry officials said on Tuesday that Vietnam would face financial difficulties in meeting the group's export plan.
All eyes were now fixed on a producer meeting in Rio de Janeiro on Thursday which is expected to discuss an African plan to slice world exports and rein in much higher prices.
Despite today's advance, robusta differential to the higher-value arabica coffee remained wide at 60 U.S. cents a lb. -- Jalil Hamid, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4985
